q: Should work-from-home emissions be counted in Scope 3 Category 7?
title: Work from home in Scope 3 Category 7
short: Yes, if you count them at all, work-from-home emissions go in Scope 3 Category 7, employee commuting. The GHG Protocol makes them optional. Include them when hybrid work is a large share of your days, or when you report lower commuting from hybrid work, so the saving is not overstated.
audience: Indian IT services firms and offices with hybrid policies

sections.h: Why it is Category 7 and not Scope 2
p: The GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard says companies may include emissions from employees teleworking in Category 7. Scope 2 covers electricity the company buys for sites in its own boundary. A home is not in your boundary and the bill is the employee's, so even if you pay a home internet or electricity allowance, the emissions stay in Scope 3.

ul: You report a fall in commuting emissions because staff come in fewer days. Leaving out the home side makes the drop look larger than it is.
A large share of working days are remote, as in many IT and BPO firms, so Category 7 would be incomplete without it.
A client, investor or rating questionnaire asks for remote work emissions by name.
You are setting a target that covers Category 7 and want the boundary fixed from the base year.

sections.h: When leaving it out is defensible
p: If few days are remote, or a screening estimate shows the figure is a small fraction of total Scope 3, you can leave it out. Say so in the methodology note: teleworking excluded, the reason, and the screening figure. Apply the same choice every year so the trend stays comparable.

ul: Business trips, hotel stays and client visits: Category 6.
A coworking desk or satellite office the company rents: report it as leased space or a purchased service, not as telework, and state which.
Laptops and furniture the company buys for home use: Category 1 or 2, depending on how you treat capital goods.

example.title: Worked example: one remote day against one office day (assumptions labelled)
lines: Office day by car, 20 km round trip at 0.154 kg CO2 per km (petrol car at 15 km per litre): 20 x 0.154 = 3.08 kg CO2
Home day without AC, about 1.16 kWh: 1.16 x 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) = 0.82 kg CO2
Home day with a 1.2 kW AC for 6 hours, 1.16 + 7.2 = 8.36 kWh: 8.36 x 0.710 = 5.94 kg CO2
Without AC the remote day saves about 2.3 kg; with AC it emits about 2.9 kg more than the drive
example.note: The car economy, home load and AC hours are assumptions. The point is that counting only the avoided commute can show a saving that is not there in summer.

senseible: Senseible records the electricity and fuel bills of your own sites. Home electricity of remote staff is not on your bills, so a teleworking estimate is something you calculate and add to your Scope 3 notes.
